name: Aseprite
category: A7. Native applications and procedural tools
role: Batch CLI and Lua scripts that export pixel-art animation, tags and sprite sheets
summary: Pixel-art and sprite animation editor. The --batch CLI converts .aseprite files to PNG sequences, GIF or sprite sheets with JSON data, and Lua scripts can create or edit sprites. Its strength is tagged frames and sheet metadata for pixel assets, not general video. Source is public but the licence is not open source.
use_when: Exporting an artist's .aseprite files to frames or a sheet with JSON metadata
Over GIMP or ImageMagick when layers, tags and frame timing must survive export
Authoring pixel-art loops that a scene plays as sprites
avoid_when: Smooth vector or high-resolution motion: Inkscape, Synfig or Blender
Sprites already exist as plain PNG frames: ImageMagick or libvips
You need an unrestricted open-source licence: use a different editor
license: Aseprite EULA: source viewable on GitHub but not open source; official binaries are paid (aseprite.org or Steam), self-build allowed under EULA terms (not read in full); some bundled modules MIT
notes: 2026-10-26: No Homebrew formula or cask exists; install is purchase or self-build. The EULA text and the macOS app path in check_command were not verified.

assessment.rationale: Releases 1.3.18.5 and 1.3.18.6 landed in September 2026 and the repository was pushed 2026-10-22. CLI batch export is documented. Licence is the Aseprite EULA, not OSI open source, and the full EULA text was not read.
